newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WMC says no flooding at Olympic Dam.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WMC says no flooding at Olympic Dam.

text.p: Copper, nickel and uranium producer WMC Ltd said on Wednesday there had been no disruption caused to its Olympic Dam copper and uranium operations from widespread flooding in the north of South Australia.

"No disruption to production or transport or our daily activities, but (flooding at the nearby Roxby Downs service town) is an inconvenience to the community," Terry Dwyer, spokesman for WMC's copper uranium division told Reuters.
Dwyer said flooding did not affect Olympic Dam's underground operations and all surface roads were sealed with tar.
Up to 250,000 kilometres of desert and pastoral land in northern South Australia have been under water in the past week following heavy rainfall throughout the region.

WMC said earlier on Wednesday its planned acceleration of the Olympic Dam mine project in South Australia was expected to cost A$1.48 billion including a A$120 million allowance for possible cost acceleration.
WMC said the acceleration of the project meant it now aimed to reach 200,000 tonnes of refined copper by the end of 1999, rather than 2001.
